page: Microsoft Azure D96d_v5 is a general-purpose server instance from the DDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 3686 GB of local storage, while containing zero GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong multi-core and memory performance alongside average single-core capabilities. The instance achieves a strong multi-core CPU score of 93235.13 in stress-ng and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17390.0, contrasted by average single-core scores in both suites. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, reaching 5037.72 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 315.9 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic capabilities are highly efficient, with the Passmark CPU encryption test placing in the top-tier category at 87610.78.

The server exhibits distinct performance tradeoffs, particularly in language model processing. While LLM prompt processing for a small 135M model is strong at 2398.76 tokens/sec, text generation for a large 70B model drops to a weak 2.69 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU accelerators. However, the instance excels in database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression, as evidenced by a strong Passmark database score of 30560.3 and a Redis SET throughput of 86.66 million operations per second. This profile makes the D96d_v5 highly suitable for relational databases, enterprise web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure D96d_v5 is a general-purpose server instance from the DDv5 family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced vector extensions. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM and 3686 GB of local storage, with no GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 93235.13 and top-tier cryptographic performance. While single-core speeds and large-scale LLM text generation are average to weak, the instance demonstrates strong memory bandwidth and database processing efficiency. It is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and static web serving.
